purpose: This lets you build Möbius maps from shifts, turns and 1/z, pin one down by three points, and then use the maps that keep the unit disk to move around the hyperbolic plane, where you measure distances and triangle angles.

stops.title: The figure
stops.text: One picture, four views. Brass rings are handles you can drag: z₁ to z₄ in view 2, the point a in views 3 and 4, and the triangle corners P, Q, R in view 4. Labels on the figure say what each color means.
stops.try: Go to step 4 and drag the corner R toward the rim. Watch the angle sum.

stops.title: Pick a view
stops.text: 1 builds a map from pieces, 2 finds the map through three points, 3 slides the disk with a disk automorphism, 4 reads the disk as the hyperbolic plane. The steps switch views for you.
stops.try: Choose view 3 and drag a around.

stops.title: Build a map
stops.text: Each button adds one piece after the ones already chosen, and the grid moves along a path of Möbius maps. The readout gives a, b, c, d, where ∞ goes, and which grid lines stay lines.
stops.try: Press Start over, then Shift: z + 1, then Invert: 1/z.

stops.title: Apply T
stops.text: T sends z₁, z₂, z₃ to 0, 1 and ∞. Slide the progress, or press Apply T, to watch the violet circle through the three points open up into the real axis.
stops.try: Drag z₃ off the circle first, then apply T again.

stops.title: The slide
stops.text: Re a, Im a and the turn θ set the disk automorphism φ. Replay the slide shows a travelling to the center while the 12 red rim points stay on the rim.
stops.try: Set Re a to 0.8 and press Replay the slide.

stops.title: Distances
stops.text: The marks 1 to 4 are one hyperbolic unit apart along a radius. They crowd toward the rim because d(0, r) = 2 artanh r grows without bound as r approaches 1.
stops.try: Compare the gap from 0 to 1 with the gap from 3 to 4.

stops.title: Move without dragging
stops.text: Choose a point, then set its real and imaginary parts with the two sliders. This does exactly what dragging does, so the lesson works from the keyboard.
stops.try: In view 4 choose R and lower its imaginary part.

stops.title: Practice
stops.text: Eight fixed problems: where ∞ goes, line or circle, the three-point map, a distance, an automorphism and an angle sum. The figure sets itself up for each one and shows the answer once you have it.
stops.try: Answer one problem wrong on purpose and read why.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Three questions that also print as an exit ticket: a concept question, a distance to compute, and a worked solution with an error to find.
stops.try: Try the spot-the-error question without the figure.

teacher: Start with step 1 and ask why every image curve passes through one point (f(∞)). In step 4 ask students to shrink the triangle and predict the angle sum. Common misconception: disk automorphisms are isometries of the hyperbolic metric, not of Euclidean distance.
